policy_title: Advocate for a permanent ceasefire and political solution in Israel and Palestine
stated: Push for an immediate and permanent bilateral ceasefire, return of hostages, a durable political solution ensuring security and equal rights for Israelis and Palestinians, recognition of the state of Palestine, and an end to illegal occupation. Investigate and prosecute war crimes and end UK arms exports to Israel.

source.quote: Green MPs will push for: • An immediate and permanent bilateral ceasefire. • A durable political solution that ensures security and equal rights for Israelis and Palestinians. This is the only way to achieve long-term security for the people of Palestine and Israel. • Recognition of the state of Palestine and an urgent international effort to end the illegal occupation of Palestinian land. • Investigation and prosecution of war crimes. • An end to all UK arms exports to and military cooperation with Israel, which make the British government complicit in these war crimes.

bearing_set.reason: Ending UK arms exports to Israel is a concrete policy action affecting UK defence-industry relationships and national security posture; ceasefire advocacy and war-crimes prosecution positions also bear directly on O5's 'national security & defence posture' and 'resilience to external threats' indicators.

UK government's formal stance on the Israel-Palestine conflict has documented domestic effects on inter-community relations, hate-crime levels, and social trust among British Muslim and Jewish communities — concrete O15 indicators.

membership_note: Policy bears on two fundamentals: O5 via national security posture and international justice, and O15 via the well-documented domestic inter-community spillovers of UK government positioning on this conflict. O9 (equal treatment) was considered — the policy explicitly invokes equal rights and due process — but those effects are internationally targeted and do not plausibly move O9 indicators for UK residents directly. O13 (prosperity via arms-export revenue) was considered but the UK arms trade with Israel is too small relative to the total to clear the non-negligible bar.
